integrity: The classification is proved symbolically from the exact divisor-sum formulas, Cohen's published prime-support/valuation criterion, multiplicative orders, and an elementary lifting-the-exponent argument. The bundled finite checker is corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem treats the prime-odd-part slice \(n=2^a p\). It does not classify \(n=2^a p^b\) for \(b>1\), the full two-distinct-prime-factor problem, or odd superharmonic numbers.
title: Superharmonic numbers with prime odd part are even perfect
